problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -3 \\ 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 5 \\ -1 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}],\,B={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c \\ d\end{aligned}]}
$$

Consider the subspace $V=\text{Col}(A)$ spanned by the columns ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}$ of the matrix $A$ and an orthogonal basis $B$ of $\text{Col}(A),$ shown above. Given that ${a}_{1}⊥{a}_{2},$ and that $B$ is derived from $V$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, what is the value of $\frac{b}{c}?$
worked_solution:
Since the first two vectors are already orthogonal, we proceed to find an orthogonal basis using the Gram-Schmidt process, as follows:

**Step 1**: We set ${v}_{1}={a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$ 

**Step 2**: We set ${v}_{2}={a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$

**Step 3**. Next, we find ${v}_{3}$ using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{3} & ={a}_{3}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{1}}\,{a}_{3}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{2}}\,{a}_{3} \\  & ={a}_{3}-\frac{{a}_{3}\cdot {v}_{1}}{{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}}{v}_{1}-\frac{{a}_{3}\cdot {v}_{2}}{{v}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}}{v}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the formula for ${v}_{3}$ in our case gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{3} & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ 5 \\ 3\end{aligned}]-(0)[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+3[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ 5 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3 \\ -3 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
\frac{b}{c}=\frac{(-2)}{(2)}=-1.
$$
